## 1. Macro regime check

**Verdict: mixed-to-cautiously-constructive, not clean-supportive.** The tape mechanics favor risk (loose conditions, tight credit, low vol, strong sector momentum with positive chip news flow today). But CPI reaccelerating from 2.66% → 4.27% alongside a rising 10Y is precisely the combination that compresses multiples on extended, high-P/E AI/semi names — the exact cohort in this universe. This supports *selective* long swing exposure, but demands unusually good entry geometry. It does not justify chasing.

## 2. Portfolio review

Empty book: $1,000 cash, zero positions, no pending orders. Nothing to HOLD or SELL_TO_CLOSE. Full flexibility.

## 3–4. Candidate scan & deep research

The whole universe has run violently — 3-month momentum ranges **+48% (TXN) to +231% (ALAB)**. That colors every entry.

- **AMD ($545)** — top-scored, but +135% in 3 months *and soaring **today** on an "AI Infrastructure Alliance" news spike* ("AMD Shares Soar…", "AMD's AI Infrastructure Push Gets Bigger"). Buying the literal spike day after a double is the worst swing entry in the group. **Pass.**
- **ALAB ($416, +231% 3m, 11.3% ATR)** and **CRDO ($267, +142% 3m, 11.3% ATR)** — parabolic and hyper-volatile; a 15%-max stop is ~1.3 ATR, pure noise range. CRDO's next earnings (listed 2026-06-01) is already stale. **Pass both.**
- **TXN ($309)** — the cleanest *business* setup: moderate +48% 3m run (analog recovery, not AI parabola), lower 5.5% ATR, smart-money conviction (D1 Capital $340M 13F), hard catalyst 2026-07-22 (~13 days). But entering 13 days pre-earnings makes this a bet on the *print*; I can't honestly claim ≥0.60 directional confidence on a binary, and the non-earnings room isn't enough to build a real 2:1. It's a coin-flip catalyst, not an asymmetric swing. **Pass.**
- **ANET ($184.85)** — highest-quality compounder (rev $1.46B→$2.0B, NI $492M→$814M, ~64% GM, steady beats), measured momentum (+18% 1m/+27% 3m, not parabolic). But it's −2.6% from its 52-week high with **no pullback to buy** and its next catalyst (earnings 8/4) is ~4 weeks out. Forcing a 2:1 from the high requires an optimistic +16% target against noise; the "asymmetric" claim is weak when you're paying the high. **Pass.**

## 5. Decision — No trade

Every proposable name requires either chasing a news spike (AMD), buying a parabola on a 15%-noise stop (ALAB/CRDO), gambling an earnings print (TXN), or paying the 52-week high with no margin of safety (ANET). To hit the mandated 2:1 R:R and ≥0.60 confidence on any of them, I'd have to back into optimistic targets I don't actually believe — the definition of a mediocre setup. Combined with the genuine macro yellow flag (CPI 2.66→4.27, 10Y rising) that specifically threatens this exact cohort, the disciplined, auditable call is to hold cash and wait for a pullback or a post-earnings reset that restores favorable entry geometry.

**Improvement note:** This run would have been materially better with two data additions to the context bundle: (1) a **forward valuation field per candidate** (P/E or EV/S vs. its own 1-yr history) — right now I'm inferring "extended" purely from price momentum, when the real question for the CPI/rate-driven multiple-compression thesis is whether valuations are stretched, and (2) **intraday/1-day price change** so I can distinguish a name resting after a run from one spiking on news *today* (AMD) without cross-referencing headline timestamps by hand. Adding a `pct_change_1d` to the price block and a `valuation` sub-object to each `top_setups` entry would sharpen entry-timing judgment on exactly the chase-vs-wait decisions that dominated this cycle.
